title: Analyses of transplanted human retinal ganglion cell morphology and localization in murine organotypic retinal explant culture
protocol: Euthanize 6- to 12-week-old mice using deep anesthesia with intraperitoneal ketamine/xylazine or CO2 asphyxiation followed by cervical dislocation.
Clasp behind the globe of each eye using Dumont #7 curved forceps.
Apply brisk outward force to enucleate eyes.
Place enucleated eyes immediately in ice cold DPBS.
Transport eyes to the dissection hood for explantation.
Explant the retina from the globe.
Puncture the sclera at the limbus using a 30-gauge needle.
Incise the sclera circumferentially just posterior to the limbus with Vannas scissors.
Grasp the sclera or residual extraocular muscle stump with Dumont Forceps #5.
Remove the cornea from the posterior eye cup by holding the eye at the limbus with forceps.
Hold the posterior cup at the optic nerve with a second pair of forceps to create traction.
Pull away the crystalline lens while securing the optic nerve with forceps.
Fold back the sclera from the retina using a pair of forceps.
Continue to use both pairs of forceps to peel back the sclera from the retina circumferentially around the limbal edge.
Evert the sclera to prolapse the retina.
Gently separate the retina from the sclera.
Secure the sclera with forceps and create four radial incisions within the retina, 90 degrees apart.
Make the final radial incision in the retina.
Detach the retina from the sclera by axotomizing RGCs at the optic nerve head with Vannas scissors.
Aspirate the free-floating retina using a P1000 pipette with a widened tip.
Transfer the retina onto the center of a culture insert, positioning it with the inner retina facing up.
Aspirate the excess PBS around the retina to allow the edges to unfold and flatten.
Use a bent vascular probe to engage overlying fluid, employing surface tension to draw folded retina peripherally.
Draw folded surfaces out using surface tension between the vascular probe and folded area to flatten retina.
Place flatmounted retina on culture membrane.
Separate the anterior and posterior segments of the globe.
Remove and discard the anterior segment including the crystalline lens.
Grasp the sclera of the posterior segment with #5 forceps.
Evert the posterior eye cup by applying pressure to the optic nerve posteriorly.
Note: This will separate the neural retina from the retinal pigmented epithelium (RPE).
Do not touch the retinal tissue with dissecting instruments.
Peel the non-retinal tissue away from the neural retina to achieve retinal isolation.
Perform dissection in a sterilized hood.
Sterilize all dissection tools prior to use and between animals.
Create 4 radial relaxing incisions in the retina from the periphery halfway to the optic nerve with Vannas scissors.
Detach the retina by cutting the optic nerve posterior to the retina using Vannas scissors.
Transfer free-floating retinas in PBS onto organotypic culture inserts using a sterile P1000 pipette with tip widened by cutting with a straight razor.
Orient the retina inside a culture insert with the RGC layer (RGCL) facing up and the photoreceptors against the membrane.
Use a P200 pipette to slowly aspirate excess PBS until the retina is flatmounted on the dry filter.
Draw the edges of retinal explant out using surface tension between the pipette tip or vascular probe and the retinal tissue.
Apply Whatman paper to the undersurface of the organotypic membrane to remove residual fluid and create suction to adhere the retinal tissue to the membrane.
Place the culture insert with the flatmounted retina in the 6-well plate.
Place the culture plate back in the incubator.
Dispense 5 μL of 0.6 U/mL Pronase onto the surface of each retina using a P10 pipette.
Visualize enzyme application onto the retinal surface under a dissecting microscope.
Start a timer for 60 min once the first retina receives the enzyme.
Return the completed 6-well plate back into the incubator before taking out the next plate for enzyme treatment.
Dry the external surface of the pipette tip prior to each application by gently wiping it with Kimwipe in a single forward motion.
Use a new box of Kimwipe for each experiment to limit contamination.
Avoid touching the surface of the Kimwipe that will contact the pipette tip.
Angle the pipette as vertically as possible, with the pipette tip aimed at the optic nerve head to ensure equal distribution of the droplet on the retinal surface.
Prepare the Inhibitor Solution during enzymatic ILM digestion.
Make the Inhibitor Solution fresh immediately prior to use.
Filter the final Inhibitor Solution with a 0.22 μm syringe filter.
Keep the Inhibitor Solution at room temperature (20°C) until use.
Add 300 μL of the Inhibitor Solution to the surface of each retina after 1 hour of enzyme treatment.
Ensure the Inhibitor Solution completely submerges the retinal tissue.
Fill the culture inserts with BSS (2 mL) to dilute the enzyme and inhibitors.
Dry the inside and bottom of the culture membrane by removing the BSS and blotting the underside with Whatman paper.
Place the plates with the culture inserts back in a 37°C incubator until the next day.
Replace 750 μl of media in each well with fresh media on the morning after explantation, several hours before RGC transplantation.
Dilute donor RGCs to the desired concentration in Retinal Explant Culture Media.
Pipette 3 μl of the cell suspension onto each recipient retina using a detailed pipetting technique.
Place the culture plates back in the incubator.
Optimize the total number of donor cells transplanted based on individual donor source and cell survival.
Limit the transplant volume to 3 μL.
Exchange retinal explant culture media every other day after RGC transplantation by replacing half of the volume (750 μL) in each well with fresh culture media.
Culture 8 × 10^3 RGCs in 150 μL of Retinal Explant Culture Media per well in a precoated 96-well plate.
Place the culture plate back in the incubator.
Allow the cells to settle onto the plate overnight (12 h).
On the following day, obtain microscopy images focusing on endogenous tdTomato expression using an epifluorescent microscope.
Alternatively, quantify cells using a vital dye such as Calcein.
Count the number of cells in each well to calculate survival rate.
Image the cell culture daily to examine RGC viability longitudinally.
Fix the retinal explants directly in the culture inserts by transferring them to new 6-well plates containing 3 mL of cold 4% PFA per well.
Add 5 mL of cold 4% PFA slowly into each culture insert to avoid detaching the retinal explants.
Maintain the fixed explants at 4°C for 1 hour.
Wash the explants by removing the PFA and replacing it with 5 mL of PBS per well.
Remove the PBS from the culture inserts after washing.
Cut the explants attached to the underlying membrane out of the culture insert using a crescent blade, creating a circumferential incision around the retinal tissue.
Transfer the retinas attached to the culture membrane into a prelabeled plate and submerge them in PBS.
Immunofluorescent staining can be performed in a 48-well plate.
Wash the retinas with PBS for 10 minutes while rocking at 80 revolutions per minute.
Block and permeabilize the tissues with blocking buffer (0.3% Triton X-100, 10% normal goat serum in PBS) for 1 hour at room temperature while rocking.
Remove blocking buffer and immerse retinas in primary antibodies diluted in blocking buffer for 2 to 5 days at 4°C while rocking.
Wash the retinas in PBS for 15 minutes while rocking; repeat 3 times.
Incubate the retinas in secondary antibodies in diluted blocking buffer overnight (12 hours) at 4°C while rocking.
Wash the retinas in PBS for 15 minutes while rocking; repeat 3 times.
Counterstain the nuclei with DAPI in PBS for 15 minutes.
Wash the retinas with PBS for 15 minutes.
Mount the retinas on membranes onto glass slides.
Add mounting medium and coverslip over the retinas.
Keep the slides in the dark to dry until imaging.
Store the slides in the dark at 4°C prior to imaging.
Perform high resolution stacked confocal images for three-dimensional volumetric analysis.
Use low magnification objectives (10× or 20×) to survey and scan across the retinal surface.
Manually focus the objective and identify the most superficial area on the entire retina.
Set this vertical position as the top of the z-stack.
Manually focus the objective and identify the deepest region of interest on the entire retina.
Set this vertical position as the bottom of the z-stack.
Perform computational volumetric and topographic analyses on donor cell survival and integration.
Set the laser power and gain for optimal exposure.
Keep the acquisition settings for master gain and digital gain constant at 650 and 1, respectively.
Adjust the laser power between 1-3 to yield optimal exposure.
Center the microscope view at the optic nerve head.
Acquire tiled z stacks with dimensions of 6 × 6 tiles for the 10× objective at 1.0× digital magnification or 11 × 11 tiles for the 20× objective at 1.0× digital magnification.
Set each tile dimension to 512 × 512 pixels for sufficient resolution.
Set the z-stack interval between 2.5–3.5 μm.
Identify a region or cell of interest with a 40× or 63× objective.
Set the top and bottom slices of the z-stack to capture the entire donor RGC from soma to the deepest neurite branch.
Ensure the bottom slice extends through the outer nuclear layer to capture the entire host neural retina for characterization.
Acquire fluorescent channels of interest.
Capture tdTomato signal.
Capture DAPI signal.
Tile images to capture entire neurite extensions if necessary.
Acquire high image resolution images for downstream 3D rendering and analyses.
Optimize image quality by increasing line averages.
Optimize image quality by decreasing scanning speed.
Use pixel dimensions of 2048 × 2048.
